  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the connection between current mitzvah observance and the future redemption is through the concept of "Yisharesh Yaakov," where drawing down the root now ensures its revelation later, and that the Targum Yonasan's interpretation of the verse as referring to redemption is primary, with the interpretation about mitzvos being secondary and following from it.</sectionSummaryBrief>

    <t s="7">is in the matter of "Yisharesh Yaakov,"</t>
    <t s="8">whose concept of drawing down the root now is that the drawing down will be in revelation,</t>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the connection between current mitzvah observance and the future redemption is through the concept of "Yisharesh Yaakov," where drawing down the root now ensures its revelation later, and that the Targum Yonasan's interpretation of the verse as referring to redemption is primary, with the interpretation about mitzvos being secondary and following from it.

translations.translation: And it is necessary to understand,
that according to the explanation above,
the connection of the observance of the commandments now
(the second interpretation)
to the redemption
(the first interpretation)
is in the matter of "Yisharesh Yaakov,"
whose concept of drawing down the root now is that the drawing down will be in revelation,
and from this that it says in the maamar
(at its beginning,
even before quoting the Targum Yonasan)
that the Targum Yonasan interprets the verse regarding the redemption,
it is understood that this is the primary interpretation,
and from this it implies that the interpretation that "Yisharesh Yaakov" refers to the observance of the commandments now comes after and in continuation of the interpretation of the Targum Yonasan,
that is,
because the observance of the commandments now comes in continuation of the general concept of the redemption.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the maamar prioritizes the interpretation of the verse as referring to the redemption because all matters are drawn from the Torah, and by prioritizing redemption in Torah it is drawn into the world, and this is reinforced by the power of thought, speech, and action, as illustrated by the Tzemach Tzedek's saying "Think good and it will be good."

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this that the maamar gives precedence to the interpretation that it refers to the redemption,
is,
because all matters are drawn from the Torah,
"He looked into the Torah and created the world,"
and by means of the fact that in the Torah the matter of the redemption is given precedence,
so too it is drawn in the world that the redemption will be with greater speed.
And to add,
that when a Jew
(and certainly a Nasi)
thinks about a good matter,
his thought causes it to be so in actuality.
As the saying of the Tzemach Tzedek that was publicized by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe,
"Think good and it will be good."
And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, related
that the Tzemach Tzedek said this saying to one of the chassidim,
and through the thought of the chassid it became good in actuality.
And it can be said,
that this that my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, added the above story,
is because by means of the fact that it occurred thus in actuality,
it is drawn also in the physical.
And in the manner of the known concept
that this that the prophets also performed actions
(in the physical)
in accordance with their prophecy,
is,
because through this the connection of the prophecy with
(the physicality of)
the world is made.
And it can be said,
that when thought comes into speech and all the more so into action,
it causes even more.
And all the more so in our case,
that in addition to this that the thought of the Tzemach Tzedek
(to give precedence to the interpretation that "The ones coming, Yaakov will take root" refers to the redemption)
came in writing
(action),
it is also a part of Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes with a prayer that through discussing these matters, especially the work of spreading Judaism and the wellsprings, the fulfillment of the prophecy of the world being filled with knowledge of God will be hastened, through the merit of the Baalei HaHilula of Teves who compiled the revealed and inner aspects of Torah.

translations.translation: May it be His will,
that through speaking about these matters they will hasten and expedite all this even more,
and particularly through the work of spreading Judaism in general and spreading the wellsprings in particular,
which is a close preparation for the fulfillment of the prophecy,
"The earth will be filled with knowledge of Havayah as the waters cover the sea,"
the conclusion and seal of the book of the Rambam
(the Baal HaHilula of the 20th of Teves),
which matter is also connected with the beginning of his book, to know that there is a First Existent.
And this is also connected with the holy book Tanya, the book of the Alter Rebbe
(the Baal HaHilula of the 24th of Teves),
in which
the matters of the knowledge of God are explained.
May it be His will that the merit of the Baalei HaHilula, who gathered and compiled in their above books all the matters of the Torah — the book Mishneh Torah which gathers
all the laws of the revealed aspect of Torah,
and the book Likkutei Amarim
(Tanya)
which compiles all the matters of the inner aspect of Torah,
and also the books Torah Or and Likkutei Torah in which the primary maamarim
of the Alter Rebbe were compiled as they were arranged by the Tzemach Tzedek — will bring near and hasten even more the fulfillment of the prophecy in the Haftarah,
"And you will be gathered one by one, O children of Israel,"
by the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself,
that very soon He will gather all of us,
and we will all go together to the Holy Land
(as it will be in an expanded manner,
"The Lord your God will expand your border")
and there itself — to Jerusalem and to the Holy Temple that will be built speedily in our days, literally.
